slides.title: Systems in Context; Approximate Solutions
slides.note: The last lesson before Friday's test, and there is no review day: hand out the Unit Review at the IXL slide; it goes home tonight. Say so out loud — no slide does.

slides.title: Warm-Up
slides.note: Q1 is yesterday in one line; Q4 is today's new reading — a crossing halfway between two grid lines. Two minutes silent, then reveal.

slides.title: Warm-Up
slides.note: Reveal. Ask for the band each question came from only if time allows.

slides.title: Vocabulary
slides.sub: The new words, before they are used.
slides.note: One phrase. An estimate is a careful read, not a guess: nearest half or tenth, the word 'about', and a check in both equations that comes out close.

slides.title: Notes
slides.note:
Each quantity is (the amount per 1)·x + (the start). The pass is \$10 at the start and \$2 for each ride: y = 2x + 10. With no pass there is no start: y = 4x. The tables come from the story too — at 0 rides the pass has already cost \$10. You may say 'slope' here; the room says 'amount per 1'.
OFF: 'What do you pay for each one? What do you pay before the first one? That is the equation.'

slides.title: Notes
slides.note:
The axes carry the story's names and a scale: rides across, cost in dollars up, one line every 4 dollars. The crossing (5, 20) is x = 5 rides and y = 20 dollars: at 5 rides both cost \$20. Check: 2(5) + 10 = 20 and 4(5) = 20. Then read the picture on either side: left of the crossing the no-pass line is lower (fewer rides — pay per ride); right of it the pass line is lower (more rides — buy the pass).
OFF: 'An answer is x and y in the story's words: 5 rides, 20 dollars.'

slides.title: Notes
slides.note:
These lines cross between x = 1 and x = 2, a little past the middle, and a little above y = 2: about (1.7, 2.3). Read to the nearest half or tenth and write 'about'. Check the estimate in both equations: 2(1.7) − 1 = 2.4 and −1.7 + 4 = 2.3 — close, not equal, which is what an estimate gives. The exact crossing is 5/3 and 7/3; nobody is asked for it (Algebra 1). A careful read of (1.5, 2.5) is also an estimate the test accepts.
OFF: 'Between which grid lines? Nearer which one? Then about, and check: close is right.'

slides.title: Example 1
slides.sub: A story to a system; the crossing in words.
slides.note: Ask for each tank's start and amount per minute before anyone writes an equation. Then read the axes' names and scale aloud: minutes across, every 2; liters up, every 10.

slides.title: Example 1
slides.note: Tank A: start 30, 5 per minute, y = 5x + 30. Tank B: y = 2x + 60. The lines cross at (10, 80): x = 10 minutes, y = 80 liters. Check: 5(10) + 30 = 80 and 2(10) + 60 = 80. Say it in the story's words. A board with 'after 80 minutes' swapped the coordinates.

slides.title: Your Turn
slides.sub: Same steps, your numbers. Boards up when done.
slides.note: Mia: y = 10x + 40; Noah: y = 5x + 100. Equal at 12 weeks: 10(12) + 40 = 160 and 5(12) + 100 = 160. Graphed with weeks every 2 and dollars every 20, the crossing is on a grid line. A board with 'after 160 weeks' swapped; one with 'after 6 weeks' set 10x + 40 = 100.

slides.title: Your Turn
slides.note: Reveal; name what a wrong board most likely did (see the note above).

slides.title: Example 2
slides.sub: A crossing halfway between grid lines.
slides.note: Ask where the lines cross before anyone says a number: between which two x's? Between which two y's? Halfway, both ways.

slides.title: Example 2
slides.note: A: y = 3x. B: y = x + 5. The lines cross halfway between x = 2 and x = 3 and halfway between the grid lines y = 6 and y = 9 (one line every 3 pages): (2.5, 7.5). This read lands exactly: 3(2.5) = 7.5 and 2.5 + 5 = 7.5. In the story: after 2.5 minutes both have printed 7.5 pages — each is halfway through its eighth page. A board with (2, 6) or (3, 9) took a nearby grid point; check it — (2, 6) is on A only: 2 + 5 = 7, not 6.

slides.title: Your Turn
slides.sub: Same steps, your numbers. Boards up when done.
slides.note: Tables at x = 0, 1, 2: 4x gives 0, 4, 8 and 2x + 3 gives 3, 5, 7. At x = 1 the first is lower, at x = 2 higher: the crossing is between, halfway — (1.5, 6). Check: 4(1.5) = 6 and 2(1.5) + 3 = 6. A board with (6, 1.5) swapped; one with (2, 8) took the grid point on one line only.

slides.title: Your Turn
slides.note: Reveal; name what a wrong board most likely did (see the note above).

slides.title: Whiteboards   ·   Question 1 of 9
slides.note: Read the crossing on the grid: x = 3 games, y = \$15 (one line every \$5). Check: 3(3) + 6 = 15 and 5(3) = 15. A board with '15 games' swapped the coordinates; one with '6 games' took the \$6 for shoes as the answer.

slides.title: Whiteboards   ·   Question 1 of 9
slides.note: Reveal. Scan the back row first; question the blank boards before the wrong ones.

slides.title: Whiteboards   ·   Question 2 of 9
slides.note: A point's meaning is its x and its y in the story's words: x = 4 miles, y = \$30 — for a 4-mile ride both taxis cost \$30. (Taxi A is y = 6x + 6 and Taxi B is y = 3x + 18: 6(4) + 6 = 30 and 3(4) + 18 = 30.) A board that says '30 miles for \$4' swapped; one that says 'Taxi A costs \$30' left out that both do.

slides.title: Whiteboards   ·   Question 2 of 9
slides.note: Reveal. Scan the back row first; question the blank boards before the wrong ones.

slides.title: Whiteboards   ·   Question 3 of 9
slides.note: The crossing is between the grid lines, so the question is only where: between x = 1 and x = 2. The tables say so without a graph — at x = 1 the second line is higher, at x = 2 the first is: they changed places in between. A board with 'between 1 and 2 for y' answered for y (y is also between 1 and 2 here — read the x); one with '2' took the nearest grid line.

slides.title: Whiteboards   ·   Question 3 of 9
slides.note: Reveal. Scan the back row first; question the blank boards before the wrong ones.

slides.title: Whiteboards   ·   Question 4 of 9
slides.note: Diagnostic on the estimate. The keyed read is about (1.3, 3.7); the exact crossing is (4/3, 11/3). One option swaps it; one is the nearest grid point, which is on one line only; one is where a line starts. On a split: sixty seconds, convince your neighbor, re-vote — then check (1.3, 3.7) in both aloud: 3.6 and 3.7, close.

slides.title: Whiteboards   ·   Question 4 of 9
slides.note: Reveal. Scan the back row first; question the blank boards before the wrong ones.

slides.title: Whiteboards   ·   Question 5 of 9
slides.note: The pattern changes: the crossing is not the answer, it is the dividing line. Before 4 hours Shop B is cheaper; after 4 hours Shop A is. At 7 hours: 3(7) + 12 = 33 and 6(7) = 42. A board with Shop B decided by the smaller start, or by the \$6 being less than \$12.

slides.title: Whiteboards   ·   Question 5 of 9
slides.note: Reveal. Scan the back row first; question the blank boards before the wrong ones.

slides.title: Whiteboards   ·   Question 6 of 9
slides.note: Diagnostic on writing the system: the amount per month multiplies x, and the one-time fee is the start. Test each option at 2 months — Gym A has cost \$40 and Gym B \$30: option C gives 50, option A gives 17 for Gym B, option B gives 60.

slides.title: Whiteboards   ·   Question 6 of 9
slides.note: Reveal. Scan the back row first; question the blank boards before the wrong ones.

slides.title: Whiteboards   ·   Question 7 of 9
slides.note: The extra-number board (ruling 22): the \$8 is not needed. The crossing is (10, 50): after 10 weeks both plants are 50 cm tall. (The sunflower is y = 4x + 10 and the bean y = 2x + 30: 4(10) + 10 = 50 and 2(10) + 30 = 50.) A board with 'after 8 weeks' used the price; one with 'after 50 weeks' swapped.

slides.title: Whiteboards   ·   Question 7 of 9
slides.note: Reveal. Scan the back row first; question the blank boards before the wrong ones.

slides.title: Whiteboards   ·   Question 8 of 9
slides.note: Backwards: the crossing's x is given, and the second plan's amount per month is missing. The first plan costs 8(6) + 30 = 78 at 6 months, so □ · 6 = 78 and □ = 13. Check: 13(6) = 78. A board with 8 copied the first plan's amount; one with 5 did 30 ÷ 6.

slides.title: Whiteboards   ·   Question 8 of 9
slides.note: Reveal. Scan the back row first; question the blank boards before the wrong ones.

slides.title: Whiteboards   ·   Question 9 of 9
slides.sub: Take your time. Boards up when you have written it.
slides.note: Written, and the exit evidence: the crossing decides. Read two aloud — one that uses the crossing, one that uses only the two costs at 10 months; both are right, and the crossing says why it will stay that way.

slides.title: Whiteboards   ·   Question 9 of 9
slides.note: Reveal. Scan the back row first; question the blank boards before the wrong ones.

slides.title: Independent Set
slides.sub: Six questions. On your own, in writing.
slides.note: Hand out the Independent Set; the same six questions are on the board. Silent work. Circulate and mark what you see; do not teach. Whatever is not finished goes home.
